abstract:
Reconstructing and analyzing single-sample regulatory networks has proven useful for understanding mechanisms of regulatory biology and its disruption in disease, but traditionally required a fair amount of programming experience and work from the user.
Here, we present SiSaNA (Single-Sample Network Analysis), a workflow that removes the need of prior programming experience and allows for single-sample regulatory network reconstruction and analysis, all via a command line interface. Using example input files, we walk the user through a tutorial on how to run the SiSaNA pipeline, interpret the results, and obtain high-quality figures summarized in a single HTML file as output.
SiSaNA is freely available to install with pip via the Python Package Index. It is additionally available on GitHub at https://github.com/kuijjerlab/sisana. Example input files can be found at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17190642.
